claims.text: The baseline coating is an unmodified FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Adding tungsten to FeNiCrCoCu promotes in situ formation of tungsten-rich intermetallic nanophases during high-temperature sliding.
Adding tungsten promotes or stabilizes a protective oxide or ceramic surface layer during high-temperature sliding.
Tungsten-rich nanophases impede dislocation motion or propagation.
The protective oxide or ceramic scale limits surface degradation at elevated temperature.
The combined nanophase and oxide-scale effects reduce microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
The combined nanophase and oxide-scale effects reduce overall sliding wear.
Relative to the baseline, the tungsten-modified coating will have lower wear-track depth under high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the baseline, the tungsten-modified coating will display fewer microscopic plastic-deformation features.
Relative to the baseline, the tungsten-modified coating will exhibit improved friction performance.
At approximately 700–900°C, oxidation and diffusion processes are active in the sliding system.
The predicted benefits are restricted to the specified high-temperature sliding regime and may differ at lower temperatures or in substantially different environments.
